concepts.preferred_label: Malignant Solitary Fibrous Tumor of the Pleura
aliases: Solitary Fibrous Tumor of the Pleura
support_spans: homogeneous right paratracheal mediastinal mass compressing and displacing the trachea to the left
11 × 8.6 × 9.5 cm lobulated solid mass arising from the right thoracic operculum/pleura
concepts.why: The presence of a large, lobulated solid mass arising from the pleura with mass effect on surrounding structures is unusual and points towards a malignant solitary fibrous tumor of the pleura.

support_spans: WBC 13.47 × 10^3/µL (85% neutrophils)
concepts.why: The elevated white blood cell count with a high percentage of neutrophils could indicate a hematologic malignancy such as lymphoma, although the presence of anisocoria is not typical for this diagnosis.

support_spans: bilateral coarse rales
11 × 8.6 × 9.5 cm lobulated solid mass arising from the right thoracic operculum/pleura
contradict_spans: homogeneous right paratracheal mediastinal mass compressing and displacing the trachea to the left
concepts.why: The presence of a large pleural mass and bilateral coarse rales could indicate pleural metastasis, although the specific characteristics of the mass are not typical for metastatic disease.

support_spans: anisocoria (right pupil 5 mm, left 3 mm)
jugular venous distension
concepts.why: The presence of anisocoria and jugular venous distension could indicate Erdheim-Chester disease, a rare histiocytic disorder that can cause a variety of systemic symptoms.

support_spans: blood pressure 200/140 mmHg
WBC 13.47 × 10^3/µL (85% neutrophils)
contradict_spans: 11 × 8.6 × 9.5 cm lobulated solid mass arising from the right thoracic operculum/pleura
concepts.why: The presence of systemic symptoms such as hypertension and elevated white blood cell count could indicate Castleman disease, a rare lymphoproliferative disorder.

support_spans: homogeneous right paratracheal mediastinal mass compressing and displacing the trachea to the left
11 × 8.6 × 9.5 cm lobulated solid mass arising from the right thoracic operculum/pleura
concepts.why: The patient's presentation with a large mediastinal mass and lymphadenopathy is concerning for lymphoma, which is a common cause of such symptoms.

support_spans: intermittent dry cough
bilateral coarse rales
concepts.why: The patient's symptoms of cough and coarse rales, along with the radiographic findings, suggest pneumonia as a possible diagnosis.

support_spans: homogeneous right paratracheal mediastinal mass compressing and displacing the trachea to the left
concepts.why: The patient's presentation with a mediastinal mass and possible lymphadenopathy could be consistent with sarcoidosis, which is a systemic granulomatous disease.

support_spans: homogeneous right paratracheal mediastinal mass compressing and displacing the trachea to the left

support_spans: homogeneous right paratracheal mediastinal mass compressing and displacing the trachea to the left
